_notes.lr: Reference is 4e-3 at global batch 512 (8 TPU replicas x 64). Scaled linearly to batch 256 -> 2e-3. Keep the lr/batch ratio if you change either; batch 512 + lr 4e-3 IS the reference config exactly and fits in 16GB with bucketing, but peaks higher on the long-clip buckets.
_notes.num_layers: Number of (3x Conv1DBlock + TransformerBlock) STAGES. 2 = reference base model at dim 192; the reference's '4x' variant is 4 stages at dim 384.
_notes.grad_clip: 0 = off, matching the reference (its clipvalue=1 is commented out). Set to 1.0 if AWP produces NaN losses.
_notes.awp_delta: The reference author reports NaN loss roughly 1 run in 5 at 0.2; 0.1 is the documented fallback. 0 disables AWP entirely and halves epoch time.
_notes.weight_decay: Decoupled. torch applies lr*wd*p and tfa applies (lr*0.1)*p, so 0.1 here reproduces the reference exactly.
_notes.diff_mode: 'forward' = reference (dx[t]=x[t+1]-x[t], reads 2 frames ahead). 'backward' = causal/streaming-safe. Changing it invalidates comparability with the reference number.
_notes.batch_size: Raised 128 -> 256 after the first timing run: peak memory was 1.9GB of 16GB, and length-bucketed batching (features.LengthBucketedBatchSampler) makes a larger batch cheaper per sample, not dearer — measured padding efficiency is 5.9x at 128 and 6.9x at 256.
_notes.num_workers: 0 = augmentation runs in-process, serialized with GPU compute (measured ~165 ms/batch of CPU work at batch 256, roughly 40% of the step once length bucketing lands). Raising it to 4 overlaps that with the GPU and should cut the step again; it is opt-in because Windows spawn is the fragile path in this repo. The dataset class lives in an importable module, so the classic Jupyter+spawn failure does not apply. >0 also switches the cache to mmap so workers share one copy instead of ~3 GB each.
